children: The three-door Thar gets a major mechanical and feature update, with deliveries starting October 11; introductory prices are valid until November 30, 2026

Mahindra & Mahindra has launched the Thar OG, the next-generation version of its three-door lifestyle SUV, at an introductory price of Rs 10.32 lakh (ex-showroom). The new model succeeds the Thar introduced in 2020 and gets changes to its platform, suspension, powertrains, off-road hardware, design and safety equipment.
Deliveries of the Thar OG will begin October 11, 2026. The introductory prices announced by Mahindra will remain valid for deliveries made until November 30, 2026.
New Platform

The Thar OG is based on Mahindra's new M_Glyde 4G platform, which the company says has been developed with higher structural stiffness. The SUV also gets a new rear PENTALINK suspension with Watts Link, along with DAVINCI Damping technology and Frequency Dependent Damping (FDD). These changes are aimed at improving ride quality, cornering stability and overall driving control, particularly compared with the outgoing three-door Thar.
The SUV also gets electric power steering, along with additional NVH damping intended to reduce noise and vibration inside the cabin.
More Powerful Engines
The Thar OG continues with three engine options, although two of them now produce more power and torque.

The 2.0-litre G20 TGDi mStallion petrol engine produces 119 kW (around 162 hp) and 330 Nm, while the 2.2-litre D22 mHawk diesel develops 111.9 kW (around 152 hp) and 330 Nm. The 1.5-litre D117 CRDe diesel continues with 87.2 kW (around 119 hp) and 300 Nm.

The D117 diesel is offered with a manual transmission and rear-wheel drive. The D22 mHawk is available with both manual and automatic transmissions, with RWD and 4WD options depending on the variant. The G20 petrol is offered with manual and automatic transmissions, with both RWD and 4WD configurations in the range.

For off-road driving, the Thar OG gets an Electronic Locking Differential (ELD) on 4WD versions. It also gets dedicated Mud, Sand and Snow terrain modes to adjust the vehicle's systems for different surfaces. RWD versions with the 2.2-litre mHawk and 2.0-litre mStallion engines also get terrain assist.
Familiar Design
Design remains familiar, but gets updated
Mahindra has retained the Thar's familiar boxy shape and upright stance, while introducing a redesigned front and rear.

The SUV gets a new grille, LED headlamps with C-shaped daytime running lights, LED fog lamps with cornering function and new LED tail lamps. The front and rear bumpers have also been redesigned, while the wider track and new R19 alloy wheels give the higher variants a different stance.

The cabin gets Truffle Brown leatherette upholstery, a leatherette-wrapped steering wheel and a soft second-row armrest with a cupholder. Other equipment includes a 26.03-cm HD touchscreen, colour MID, wireless charging, cruise control, Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, rear-view camera and a tyre-pressure monitoring system.
The Thar OG will also be available in two new exterior colours — Artemis Silver and Jeans Blue — alongside six existing colours.
Six airbags and four-wheel disc brakes
Safety equipment has also been upgraded. The Thar OG gets six airbags, including four Head Pelvis Thorax Shoulder (HPTS) airbags for front and rear occupants.

Higher variants get disc brakes on all four wheels, while the SUV is equipped with Mahindra's ESP 9.3 suite with rollover mitigation. Front parking sensors, a rear-view camera and tyre-pressure monitoring are also available.
The entry-level AXT continues with front disc and rear drum brakes, while the ZXT gets front and rear disc brakes.
